definition: The reaction of an ion from a dissolved salt with water, forming $\ce{H3O^+}$ or $\ce{OH^-}$ ions; ions whose parent acid or base is weak do this, such as $\ce{NH4^+}$ (acidic) and $\ce{CH3COO^-}$ (basic), while ions from strong parents, such as $\ce{Cl^-}$ and $\ce{Na^+}$, do not.

The flatter part of a pH curve where a weak acid and its conjugate base (or a weak base and its conjugate acid) are both present, so the pH changes slowly; at its middle, the half-equivalence point, $\mathrm{pH} = \mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}$ (or $\mathrm{pOH} = \mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{b}$).
